messages:
maria-dev: heads up — since the keystore IAM conditional policy rolled last night, we're seeing a bunch of GPU nodes stuck in PROVISIONING with KMS decrypt failures.
maria-dev: example from node-az1-07: `failed to decrypt keystore: AccessDeniedException` and audit shows conditional:SourceIp mismatch
liam-infra: looking. did we push fw/privatelink changes in eu-west last night? I deployed 1723-privnet-rule around 23:10 UTC
liam-infra: PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/compare/1723-privnet-rule — it tightened allowedSubnetList for keystore
raj-sre: alert just fired for high provision latency on gpu-pool-eu — spike started ~00:12 UTC. autoscaler kept retrying nodes -> cost + throttled warm pools
oncall-bot: Alert: GPU_PROVISION_DURATION > 15m for pool gpu-pool-eu (count: 42) — triggered at 4012345705
maria-dev: ok — hypothesis: keystore policy denies decrypt from some privatelink ENIs -> kubelet cannot fetch node secrets -> node stays unsched
julie-security: confirmed partial deny in the policy for subnet tags `privnet:edge` — it was intentional to block hostpath keystore access for legacy subnets
julie-security: but audit-shipper/service-account needs decrypt for logshipper and the canary auth role — we should exempt that principal for now
sam-cost: note — stuck nodes are incurring reserved startup (spot fallback) and push cost ~ $6k/day if not cleared. we should triage fast
liam-infra: mitigation plan: 1) add `arn:aws:iam::acct:role/audit-shipper` to keystore allowed principals 2) temporarily widen allowedSubnetList to include privnet-legacy for 30m 3) restart pending nodes
liam-infra: quick config snippet I used in staging (apply to keystore-policy):
```
- Effect: Allow
  Principal: arn:aws:iam::acct:role/audit-shipper
  Condition:
    IpAddress: { aws:SourceIp: ["10.20.0.0/16"] }
```
raj-sre: can we do a 5% canary before global widening? want to avoid opening path permanently
maria-dev: canary sounds right. liam — can you scope to one az and attach an explicit tag so autoscaler targets canary nodes only?
liam-infra: yes — will patch policy + label nodes `keystore-canary=true` and set pool min=1 for az1, then monitor 15m
julie-security: also add an audit log allow rule so we don't lose decrypt audit events: keystore-audit-service principal must be unaffected
maria-dev: after canary looks green I'll drain and reprovision the 40 stuck nodes
raj-sre: monitoring: watch `kubelet.decrypt_errors` and `node.provision_time` and autoscaler retries; I'll post metrics in 10m
sam-cost: created ENG-PLAT-928 ticket to track cost impact and follow-up permanent policy rollback/PR with better subnet mapping
maria-dev: thanks — doing the patch now. tagging @julie-security for postmortem and fix PR
julie-security: ack. we'll follow up with a tighter least-priv policy in a week + a review of privnet tag coverage :thumbsup:
liam-infra: patch applied to canary az at 4012345752, restarting pending nodes
raj-sre: canary node succeeded and joined at 4012345790. decrypt errors dropped to 0 in that az
maria-dev: rolling remainder now. will update ticket when all nodes back
sam-cost: noted — moving to priority-1 billing watch
maria-dev: TY everyone :rocket:
